suggestions.topic: Python AsyncIO vs Threading: When to Stop Blocking
suggestions.rationale: Developers continually confuse I/O-bound concurrency with CPU-bound parallelism, leading to locked event loops and poor application throughput.
suggestions.hook_angle: Your Python API is freezing up under load because you're using threads where AsyncIO was meant to rule—let's fix your event loop.

suggestions.rationale: System design interview candidates frequently fail to explain how cascading failures occur and how circuit breakers gracefully degrade service.

suggestions.topic: Cracking the Distributed Systems Architecture Interview
suggestions.rationale: High-stakes technical interviews test architectural intuition on scalability, partition tolerance, and consistent hashing under tight constraints.
suggestions.hook_angle: Most senior system design interviewees fail not because of coding, but because they design single points of failure in distributed topologies.

suggestions.topic: Decoding Python's Memory Management & Garbage Collection
suggestions.rationale: Memory leaks in long-running Python microservices puzzle even mid-level engineers who don't understand reference counting and cyclic garbage collection.

suggestions.topic: Implementing a Circuit Breaker in Distributed Apps
suggestions.rationale: Engineers struggle to transition from theoretical circuit breaker states (Closed, Open, Half-Open) to production-ready failure thresholds.

suggestions.topic: Mastering the AsyncIO Event Loop Queue in Python
suggestions.rationale: Implementing producer-consumer patterns asynchronously requires deep knowledge of asyncio.Queue, avoiding race conditions without locking.
suggestions.hook_angle: Stop using standard Python queues inside async functions; you are blocking the entire event loop and destroying your concurrency.
